primary.citation: Puglielli & Cabdallah Cumar Mansuur. 1997. Grammatica della lingua somala per le scuole medie superiori, section 6.3.2.1, grammar pp. 97-98 (PDF pp. 98-99); John I. Saeed. 1999. Somali, section 4.3.4.3 Past simple, p. 86.
primary.evidence: The already-reviewed Conjugation-2 morphophonology records Puglielli & Cabdallah Cumar Mansuur's explicit 2SG past waad joogi-s-ay, decomposed as joogi+t+ay, together with the rule that t changes to s after an i-final stem. The same reviewed source also prints wey kari-s-ay as kari+t+ay, independently exposing the t-bearing 3SG feminine past cell. Saeed's explicit C2A past-simple table independently supplies the already-active plural cells 2PL kariseen and 3PL kariyeen. These development facts predate the corresponding benchmark answer lookups and no benchmark answer surface is used as runtime evidence.

independent_corroboration.citation: Zorc et al. Somali textbook, Chapter 11 Second Conjugation Verbs, p. 85; GiellaLT Somali morphophonology documentation.
independent_corroboration.evidence: The C2A kari paradigm independently prints second-person singular karisey/karisay, second-person plural kariseen, and third-person plural kariyeen, and explicitly describes the second-conjugation t-to-s change in the 2SG/3SGF cells. This corroborates the class mechanics without using buuxisay, caafisay, bushisay, or any other frozen target answer source.

first_plural_independent.citation: Martin Orwin. 1995. Colloquial Somali: A Complete Language Course. Routledge.
first_plural_independent.evidence: Orwin independently gives C2A kari 1PL past karinnay and describes the first-person-plural n as geminated in this weak-causative pattern. Runtime authorization therefore uses agreement n plus past ay together with the already-reviewed i+n -> inn process. This development fact is distinct from the frozen v16 Green 2021 answer row; buubinnay is never used to author the rule. Orwin's frozen v6 answer rows are also not used as runtime evidence.
first_plural_independent.benchmark_boundary: v16 Green 2021 buubinnay remains evaluation-only; v6 benchmark answers remain evaluation-only

first_singular_independent.citation: Martin Orwin. 1995. Colloquial Somali: A Complete Language Course, General past C2A table, p. 51. Routledge; Zorc & Issa Somali Reference Grammar index, C2A kari entries referring to p. 79.
first_singular_independent.evidence: Orwin's explicit general-past C2A table gives kari + ay -> kariyay for 1SG and the same kariyay surface for 3SG masculine, and states that y is inserted between stem-final i and a. The Zorc reference grammar independently indexes kariyey as both 1SG past and 3SG masculine past. This independently authorizes the syncretic 1SG/3SG-masculine structure as empty agreement plus past ay using the already-reviewed i-vowel-glide process. The previously live 1SG analysis is retained and the newly activated 3SG masculine analysis is added as a second candidate for the same surface. Frozen v17 aaddiyay/buufiyay and frozen v18 aammusiyay/abhiyay answer rows are not used to author this rule.
first_singular_independent.orthography_note: Orwin prints -ay spelling (kariyay); Zorc also indexes the -ey variant kariyey. The existing project policy continues to defer broad ay/ey variant activation.
first_singular_independent.benchmark_boundary: v17 and v18 target answers remain evaluation-only; runtime authority comes from the pre-v18 Orwin/Zorc class evidence

third_singular_feminine_independent.citation: Puglielli & Cabdallah Cumar Mansuur. 1997. Grammatica della lingua somala per le scuole medie superiori, section 6.3.2.1, grammar pp. 97-98 (PDF pp. 98-99); Zorc et al. Somali textbook, Chapter 11 Second Conjugation Verbs, p. 85.
third_singular_feminine_independent.evidence: The pre-v19 reviewed Puglielli evidence explicitly prints wey kari-s-ay and analyzes the C2A past ending as kari+t+ay with t changing to s after stem-final i. Zorc independently states that the same second-conjugation t-to-s alternation applies in the 2SG and 3SG feminine cells. This authorizes 3SG feminine as agreement t plus past ay through the already-reviewed i_t_assibilation process. Because 2SG uses the same underlying morphology, both person analyses must be retained for the same -isay surface.
third_singular_feminine_independent.benchmark_boundary: Frozen v19 caafisay and bushisay remain evaluation-only and are not used to author or special-case the runtime rule.

benchmark_isolation.note: The 3SG feminine rule is activated from pre-v19 Puglielli/Zorc class development evidence for the t-bearing 3SG-feminine cell and i+t assibilation. Frozen v19 caafisay and bushisay remain evaluation-only and no target-specific profile is added. All eleven activated C2A class lemmas receive the same narrow seven-cell past authority, with 1SG/3SG-m and 2SG/3SG-f syncretisms preserved as separate analyses, no open-class generation, and no correction authority.

notes: Narrow generic C2A class-level past activation for the complete seven-person staged set over the reviewed 11-lemma allowlist. 1SG and 3SG masculine are syncretic and both use empty agreement plus past ay with the reviewed i-vowel glide. 2SG and 3SG feminine are syncretic and both use agreement t plus past ay with reviewed i+t assibilation, yielding -isay while remaining separate analyses for the same surface. 1PL uses agreement n plus past ay with the reviewed weak-causative i+n -> inn alternation; 2PL uses stem + s + een; 3PL uses the reviewed i-vowel glide before een. Mechanical generated outputs are recognition/analysis candidates only, are not claims of independent attestation, and never receive automatic correction authority. This does not claim open-class or all-orthography past coverage.
